header: Date: 2026-09-21 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Riley Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Nova Health), Priya Rao (Nova Infra), Miguel Santos (Nova CTO)
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on Dedicated sizing and autoscaling policies. Reviewed recent pilot results, discussed burst behavior and warm pool sizing, agreed to run a 24-hour burst test and update sizing sheet. Action items assigned for logs, sizing, and scheduling technical deep dive.
topics: Recent pilot results: latency P50/P95, failures during 2x spike
Autoscaling policy design: min reserved, warm pool, burst nodes
Burst planning: 4x traffic simulation and cost implications
KV cache and prefix caching impact on latency
Security/compliance ask: SOC2 excerpts and audit logs
transcript: [00:00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining today. We'll run through the runbook items and then dig into the burst testing plan.
[00:00:08] Jordan Lee: Thanks, Avery. Quick note - we had that spike on Friday that pushed P95 to about 1.2s for the generation endpoint, wanted to get aligned on mitigation.
[00:00:18] Riley Patel: Yeah I pulled the logs, saw a combo of cold starts plus KV cache misses, plus one pod that OOM'd during the peak, so it amplified latency.
[00:00:27] Priya Rao: We also saw some schedule jitter on the autoscaler, it took maybe 60s to spin up additional instances which didn't help the tail.
[00:00:36] Miguel Santos: Right, our SLA target is P95 < 500ms for interactive flows; the current numbers are too high during bursts.
[00:00:45] Avery Chen: Understood. Today we'll review the sizing sheet we sent, talk about reserved capacity vs burst, and nail down the 24h burst test Riley will run.
[00:00:55] Jordan Lee: Quick Q - what's the recommended warm pool size? We don't want to overprovision for cost reasons.

[00:01:02] Riley Patel: For models of your size (13B quantized) we typically suggest a warm pool that covers steady-state peak QPS plus headroom for 30-50% short bursts. For your observed peaks, that maps to 3 reserved nodes and a warm pool of 1-2 additional nodes before autoscale kicks in.
[00:01:20] Priya Rao: How does the warm pool differ from burst nodes? I thought warm pool meant pre-warmed KV caches.

[00:01:26] Riley Patel: Good point - warm pool here means nodes pre-attached with warmed KV cache and loaded kernels so cold-start is minimal. Burst nodes are additional ephemeral nodes that may have a slightly higher cold-start cost depending on provisioning path.
[00:01:38] Miguel Santos: Ok so if we set reserved to 3 and warm pool 2, then burst up to 6 total, that gives us 2x headroom. But Friday's spike was around 4x.
[00:01:50] Avery Chen: That's why we want to run the 24h 4x burst test - to see how autoscaler behaves and quantify cold-starts and tail latency under sustained high load versus short spikes.
[00:02:00] Jordan Lee: Sounds good. Can Riley also capture KV cache hit rates and token-level cost during the test?
[00:02:06] Riley Patel: Yep, I'll instrument the run to capture KV hit rate, P50/P95/P99 latency, cold start counts, and per-token cost estimates. I'll also surface kernel selection logs.
[00:02:15] Priya Rao: One concern - during the Friday spike a single pod OOM'd; do we need to change the headroom or memory settings per container?
[00:02:23] Riley Patel: We'll review container memory limits; there may have been a config mismatch in the pod's resource requests. I'll run through the pod memory usage and share recommendations.
[00:02:33] Miguel Santos: Also curious about throttling fallback - if Dedicated capacity is saturated, can Redwood route to a cheaper model variant or hosted fallback?

[00:02:41] Avery Chen: Yes, we can set routing policies - fallbacks to a quantized variant or a regional hosted pool. But for this pilot you wanted Dedicated isolation, so we'll keep fallbacks as an emergency option and capture the failover behavior.
[00:02:55] Jordan Lee: Let's talk about autoscaler timing - Priya said it was about 60s to add nodes. Can that be shortened?

[00:03:02] Riley Patel: There are a few levers: increase warm pool, use burst pre-warmed images, or tweak the autoscale policy to scale more aggressively (lower cool-downs, scale per queued requests). Aggressive policies cost more but reduce tail.
[00:03:13] Priya Rao: We prefer to optimize cost first, but we need consistent user experience. We can accept short tail increases if P95 stays close to target except during true outages.

[00:03:22] Avery Chen: For the sizing sheet I'll include scenarios: conservative (min nodes + small warm pool), balanced (your expected steady + warm pool), aggressive (larger warm pool to eliminate cold starts). Each will show cost and expected P95 impact.
[00:03:34] Jordan Lee: Perfect. Also, Miguel mentioned compliance - we need SOC2 excerpts and details on audit log retention for the Dedicated control plane.
[00:03:42] Avery Chen: I'll attach our SOC2 summary and the audit log retention doc. Riley, can you add a note about where logs live during the burst test and how we capture them?
[00:03:50] Riley Patel: Yep I'll enable export to the customer's S3 and include a manifest of the logs: latency, kernel selection, KV cache metrics, autoscaler events.
[00:03:58] Miguel Santos: Cool. On the pricing side, how are burst nodes billed? Per-minute or hourly?

[00:04:04] Avery Chen: Burst nodes are billed per-minute with a small granularity; reserved nodes are profiled into committed monthly cost. The sizing sheet will show blended cost estimates for the scenarios.
[00:04:13] Priya Rao: When you say blended, do you include cache-hit savings and quantization effects?
[00:04:18] Riley Patel: Yes, the model-run cost section will show baseline per-token cost, and adjusted cost with prefix caching and quantization that you configured.
[00:04:26] Jordan Lee: For the 24h run, can we schedule it during a low-traffic window to avoid impacting customers? We want representative traffic but not during business hours.
[00:04:33] Miguel Santos: We prefer overnight in our timezone - Jordan, can you confirm a window?
[00:04:38] Jordan Lee: I'll propose a Thursday 02:00-02:00 UTC window in the thread after this call.
[00:04:44] Avery Chen: Sounds good. Riley, make sure the test has a gradual ramp up to 4x and then some randomized spikes so we capture autoscaler reaction.
[00:04:50] Riley Patel: I'll do a 10m ramp, 4h sustained at 4x, then randomized bursts every 30m for the 24h - that should exercise both scale-up and cooldown behavior.
[00:04:59] Priya Rao: Any notes on kernel selection? We saw different kernels on Friday depending on sequence length.
[00:05:05] Riley Patel: Kernel selection depends on seq len and hardware. I'll capture which kernels were chosen and whether any fallback kernels triggered; that helps tune compilation settings.
[00:05:13] Miguel Santos: If we end up needing more headroom permanently, what's the procurement timeline for Dedicated capacity?
[00:05:19] Avery Chen: For Reserved Dedicated nodes, typical lead time is 2-4 weeks for provisioning and configuration. We can provision trial burst capacity faster for the pilot as ephemeral nodes.
[00:05:28] Jordan Lee: Ok - last question: will the test affect data residency or encryption behavior? We have strict constraints for some customers.
[00:05:34] Avery Chen: No change - Dedicated control plane respects KMS/HSM and VPC options. I'll include the KMS integration note in the docs I send.
[00:05:42] Riley Patel: Also, I'll capture audit events and show how to pull them from the control plane during the test.
[00:05:48] Priya Rao: Great. Anything else before we wrap?

[00:05:50] Avery Chen: Quick recap: Riley runs the 24h burst test and sends logs; Avery updates sizing/pricing and SOC2 + audit docs; Jordan shares traffic histograms and confirms the test window; schedule deep dive next Tue. I'll send a summary and calendar invites after this.
[00:06:05] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone, looking forward to the results.
[00:06:08] Miguel Santos: Thanks.
[00:06:10] Avery Chen: Thanks team, talk soon.
